claims.statement: 66 actual guarded original/candidate commands under three hash seeds recover from four complete 5313-input regular Git supplied graphs. 8 typed/literal and 3 raw compatibility sources distinguish retained capture/mark/entry-named/raw continuations from consumed typed entry groups. Authored cumulative occurrence pieces, actual callback arguments/scalar context/error effects, parser argument references/frames and complete Toolbox channels pass independent review with 10 effective evidence/authority RED controls. Original production remains unchanged. The selected output-emission and callback-identity protocol is unimplemented and unverified. The initial seven-owner declaration rejection retains its exact staged delta and every original claim/input identity; pending nodes use planning metadata.
claims.scope: Bounded diagnosis and future repair selection, not production GREEN, generated-output transfer acceptance, arbitrary opaque-callback proof, full Phase0, readiness, other-backend or global audit closure. Raw compatibility probes measure substitution/AST/producer paths only, not reference-value execution. Typed group [null] is a nullable baseline, not a non-null result promise. Literal replacement/readiness retain separate existing owners. Complete ordinary/emitted/native/fresh typed channels and original rejected-candidate channels remain distinct. The exact full regular supplied superset is recoverable from immutable Git blobs/modes plus declared authored overlays; gitlinks and nonregular payloads are excluded without inspection. Necessary read-only OS/Perl/Python/Git standard-library prerequisites are external; no cross-host reproducibility claim is made. Every project-owned output remains repository-volume rooted. Existing public book teaching remains accurate and unchanged. Future actual producer RED/GREEN, source inverses, adversarial callback/nested/literal controls, complete Phase0/direct consumers and independent canonical replacement admission remain required. The exact initial declaration failure is an unadmitted preparation, independently recovered with an isolated same-volume index/object store while preserving the real index.
